summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a recent AV fistula revision was readmitted for persistent low-grade fevers and an episode of slurred speech reported during dialysis. The slurred speech was attributed to severe dry mouth, with neurologic imaging showing no acute stroke but chronic microvascular changes; she was started on aspirin for secondary prevention. Fevers lacked a clear infectious source—blood cultures were negative, the fistula site was clean, and no pneumonia was seen on imaging. Elevated liver enzymes and biliary duct dilation on MRCP suggested possible biliary dysfunction as a fever source, leading to ursodiol initiation. Her cardiac function showed worsening valvular regurgitation, contributing to exertional shortness of breath. She remained afebrile off antibiotics for over 48 hours, was clinically stable, and discharged home with follow-up arranged in cardiology, gastroenterology, rheumatology, and ENT for an ear canal lesion noted on CT.
